Article Title: 'Slippages reveal design flaw on Kanpur-Lucknow e-way'
Article Text:
Slippages on Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway point to design issue, not construction defect; stretches will need bottom-up rebuild. (AI-generated image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Slippages on sections of the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway within days of its inauguration point to a design issue, not a construction defect, a top govt official has said, adding that simple patchwork repairs will not solve the problem. "The affected stretches will have to be rebuilt bottom up. We need to ensure there is no laxity at the designing stage of projects. This is a major concern for us, especially since the expressway has been executed under Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM)," the official said.The Centre is awaiting the final report of an expert who conducted a detailed investigation into the slippages. "There was no deficiency in the thickness of the road or in the pavement layers beneath it," the official added. In HAM projects, the private developer is responsible for the operation and maintenance of the project through the entire concession period, which, typically, is 15 years.A preliminary investigation by an IIT Kharagpur professor had identified the use of weak, highly plastic soil beneath parts of the expressway as one of the main reasons for the slippages. Plastic soil loses strength when wet and can get deformed under load. The preliminary report shows poor drainage as a contributing factor.
Article Summary: Slippages on Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway point to design issue, not construction defect; stretches will need bottom-up rebuild. "We need to ensure there is no laxity at the designing stage of projects," top govt official says.

Apple's next-generation smartwatches could bring a major change to health tracking. The change could offer users a more granular look at how their heart rate changes across different activities and times of day.Apple is also reportedly working on a redesigned health and fitness experience for its watches. The company is said to be exploring ways to present wellness information in a simpler and easier-to-understand format, similar to dedicated fitness platforms such as Whoop and Oura.Rather than focusing mainly on individual workouts or occasional readings, the updated experience could offer users a broader picture of how their body responds over the course of a day.Health tracking may not be the only change coming to Apple's smartwatch lineup. Gurman reports that Apple is testing a ceramic version of the Apple Watch Series 12, which could be offered in white and dark grey finishes.The company is also believed to be preparing new watch band colours and configurations for the upcoming models. Article Title: VerSe Innovation launches SparkStation at Film Expo 2026
Article Text: VerSe Innovation has launched SparkStation at Film Expo 2026 - an AI content operating system that carries an entire production from first idea to final cut inside a single system. The company claims that SparkStation is VerSe's first global-first offering and one of the largest product bets the company has ever made. The platform is backed by $30+ million in committed investment over 24 months, spanning GPU infrastructure, proprietary AI orchestration, and specialist talent aiming to serve 100+ studios, 1,000+ brands and thousands of creators globally. Commercial models span credits for creators, seat-based SaaS for studios and brands, and enterprise licensing with API access.In a press release, the company stated that SparkStation rolls out in three phases: beta access (August 29), general availability (October 1), and enterprise API tier (November 1). It said that SparkStation is one platform built for three verticals:•Filmmakers and production houses: With capabilities that include, story builder, script coverage, casting, location design, storyboards, shot creation, music and dialogue generation, editing and rendering, with clean exports into industry-standard NLEs so that filmmakers retain control.•Brands, Businesses, E-commerce and Agencies: With image, video, UGC and performance ad formats, catalogue-scale product creative, and hundreds of localised, platform-reframed variants per campaign produced in hours rather than weeks.•Creators and influencers: With lots of templates and studio-grade output on a credits model.It delivers on five differentiators that compound:•An operating system, not a tool: Every stage of production in one pipeline. Unlike other platforms that generate mere clips, SparkStation delivers complete, coherent, continuous & consistent creative outputs.•Production-grade continuity across 5 locked elements: Face, expression, wardrobe, location & props, held across an entire production rather than a single shot. Continuity is the precise reason AI video has not crossed into professional workflows & SparkStation solves all of these 5 elements.•Model-agnostic orchestration: SparkStation routes each task - a face, a crowd, a camera move, a voice, a language to whichever model is best at it. Multiple models from every major provider sit behind one interface and each creative task is routed to the one that's best at it.•60+ languages at production fidelity: The performance travels and not just the words - lip movements, emotional beats and local idioms. Six weeks of localisation becomes one day.•Built by creators, for creators: Designed by a team drawn from film, VFX and gaming as much as from AI research with no lock-in and native exports to Premiere, Final Cut and DaVinci Resolve. Studios integrate with the NLEs while maintaining continuity across multi-language films. Brands produce infinite creative variants at fraction of traditional timelines. Agencies scale client deliverables. Creators access a full-service studio without infrastructure overhead.Umang Bedi, Co-Founder & CEO, VerSe Innovation, said “SparkStation is VerSe's first global offering and one of the single largest product bets VerSe has made. Production cost has been the invisible ceiling on what stories get made. When you solve that constraint, you don't simply make content cheaper. You make content that never cleared the production threshold before. That is what we are solving for - not efficiency, but possibility. SparkStation has been used internally for over 6 months now at scale delivering unprecedented speed and economics. Spark is not a platform in testing it is in production, at scale, generating revenue”.

Article Title: Anthropic has a warning for Claude users: We have recently seen some ...
Article Text:
What Anthropic told affected users

The malware behind the attacks

How Anthropic is responding

Poll Vote & Share your view Have you ever experienced unauthorized access to an online account? Yes, multiple times Yes, once No, never 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

What Anthropic is telling users to do

AI giant Anthropic has issued a warning to Claude users after discovering that infostealer malware is hijacking active login sessions to access accounts and drain usage. According to a report by Bleeping Computers, the company said that the attackers are stealing authenticated browser sessions from infected computers, enabling them to bypass passwords and two-factor authentication. Anthropic is signing affected users out of Claude, removing saved payment methods, and refunding unauthorised chargesIn an email sent to affected accounts, Anthropic said it recently became aware of a bad actor using common infostealer malware to steal Claude login sessions directly from people's computers, then using those stolen sessions to access accounts and burn through the victims' usage. The email, which was shared publicly on Reddit by one affected user, also gave people a way to recognise the symptom: if a Claude account's usage limits appeared to refill and then mysteriously drain while the account wasn't actively being used, that pattern was likely the cause.The mechanics of the attack make it particularly hard to notice. Infostealer malware can copy an already-authenticated browser session, meaning an attacker doesn't need to go through a normal password or two-factor authentication login process to gain access — they simply reuse a session that's already been verified.Anthropic said its investigation is still ongoing, but that affected computers were most likely already infected with general-purpose infostealer malware unrelated to Claude itself.The company was explicit on this point, stating it has no reason to believe the malware is connected to Claude, was installed through Claude, or relates to anything the user did within the Claude platform.According to Anthropic, this type of malware typically spreads through downloads or malicious apps, and once installed, harvests information stored locally on a device — including browser passwords, login cookies, and credentials tied to a wide range of other apps and services. A user's Claude session was likely just one of many pieces of data swept up in that broader collection process, with attackers only recently beginning to specifically extract and exploit the Claude sessions from what they'd already gathered.In the case shared on Reddit, the affected user confirmed they had downloaded a pirated game shortly before the compromise, offering a likely explanation for how the malware ended up on their system in the first place.Anthropic said it has identified several specific malware families involved in these attacks, including Vidar, LummaC2, StealC, RedLine, and Acreed on Windows systems, along with Atomic Stealer (AMOS) affecting a small number of Mac users.For accounts identified as compromised, Anthropic is taking several protective steps: signing affected users out of Claude, revoking the stolen sessions, removing any saved payment methods from the account, and refunding charges it identifies as unauthorized.However, the company was clear that this response only addresses the symptom, not the underlying cause. Anthropic warned that signing a user out stops the stolen session from being used, but it doesn't remove the malware itself — meaning if the infection is still present on a user's device, their very next login session could be stolen through the exact same method.Anthropic has urged affected users to take basic follow-up security steps beyond what the company can do on its end, including changing their account credentials, revoking any other active sessions tied to their accounts, and thoroughly removing the malware from their infected computers before logging back in.
Article Summary: AI giant Anthropic has issued a warning to Claude users after discovering that infostealer malware is hijacking active login sessions to access accounts and drain usage. Anthropic is signing affected users out of Claude, removing saved payment methods, and refunding unauthorised charges.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness.

Article Title: Fraudster uses Raigad SP’s WhatsApp display photo to dupe police staff, seeks Rs 50,000
Article Text:
A cyber fraudster impersonated Raigad SP on WhatsApp, targeting police personnel for money transfers, but the scam attempt was foiled. (AI-generated image)





NAVI MUMBAI: Raigad Cyber Police have registered a case against an unidentified fraudster who allegedly used the WhatsApp Display Picture (DP) of Raigad Superintendent of Police (SP) Anchal Dalal to deceive several police personnel into transferring money.On Thursday, the fraudster sent a message to Raigad SP's reader, PSI Siddheshwar Murkute, asking him to transfer money urgently. Murkute immediately realised that it was a modus operandi commonly used by cyber scammers, as the WhatsApp message was sent from an international number that was not saved in his mobile phone.Thereafter, PSI Murkute learnt that the same scammer had sent similar messages to several Raigad police personnel. Fortunately, no one fell prey to the fraud, as the police personnel were aware of this modus operandi used by cyber fraudsters.Subsequently, PSI Murkute registered an FIR against the unidentified accused under the relevant section of the BNS for the offence of cheating by personation.The complainant, PSI Murkute, said, "I had received the WhatsApp message from an international number and the DP was of Raigad SP Anchal Dalal.The message read, 'I am in a meeting and my mobile is switched off. Immediately transfer Rs 50,000 to my bank account.' I knew the message sender was a scammer. I deliberately replied asking for the bank account number by pretending to send the money. As I received the bank account number from the scammer, it will be useful for the cyber police team to trace the bank account holder. "PSI Murkute added, "One police officer had received a WhatsApp message from the same international number asking to transfer Rs 2,000 by impersonating SP madam and claiming that it was required for filling diesel in the car, and that her mobile battery had drained and she was unable to pay online at the fuel station."API Amol Jadhav of Raigad Cyber Police said, "The cyber scammers use VPNs (Virtual Private Networks) to mask their identity. However, the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the WhatsApp number used by the accused will be obtained to trace the location, and the accused will soon be behind bars."
Article Summary: A cyber fraudster impersonated Raigad SP on WhatsApp, targeting police personnel for money transfers. Fortunately, no one fell prey to the fraud, as the police personnel were aware of this modus operandi used by cyber fraudsters. One police officer received a WhatsApp message from the same international number asking to transfer Rs 2,000 by impersonating SP madam.

Article Title: ANPR camera system launched in Namakkal district to curb traffic violations
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: An automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) camera system was launched in Namakkal district on Monday to impose fines on traffic violators. The facility was inaugurated at the Namakkal–Salem Road corner junction by district superintendent of police Yadav Krish Ashok.The ANPR system will automatically detect violations such as using mobile phones while driving, riding w-wheelers without helmets and driving without seat belts. Fines will be issued digitally. The penalty amount and receipt will be sent directly to the violator’s registered mobile number.Speaking to reporters, S P Yadav Krish Ashok said, “Road accidents have claimed 348 lives in Namakkal district in the past eight months. Strict monitoring is essential to reduce fatalities. The ANPR camera system will help enforce discipline among motorists. Riders must wear helmets for their own safety and that of their families. Those indulging in reckless stunts will also be closely monitored and penalised.”
Article Summary: The facility was inaugurated at the Namakkal–Salem Road corner junction by district superintendent of police Yadav Krish Ashok. A remarkable hoard of 2,600 silver coins has been discovered inside a small ceramic jug in Kolomna, offering a rare glimpse into medieval Russian wealth. Archaeologists from the Institute of Archaeology of the Russian Academy of Sciences found the hoard during rescue excavations in the historic centre of the city, near the Kremlin. The coins date mainly to the reigns of Grand Princes Vasily I Dmitrievich and Vasily II Vasilyevich the Dark, with the newest pieces dating to the second half of the 1420s. Researchers say the hoard may also have been concealed during an epidemic that swept through cities of Rus' between 1425 and 1427. The discovery is the largest complete collection of coins from the first half of the 15th century available to researchers. Its contents could help researchers understand wealth, trade and how money was used in medieval Kolomna.The hoard was found in Kolomna's historic centre during rescue excavations by the Moscow Region expedition of the Institute of Archaeology of the Russian Academy of Sciences. Archaeologists discovered a ceramic jug painted with engobe inside a shallow natural pit on the city's posad(town), close to the Kremlin.There were more than 2,600 silver dengi, the main denomination represented in the collection. The find is considered the largest complete coin hoard from the first half of the 15th century available for study. The quantity and remarkable variety of the coins make the hoard especially valuable for understanding how money circulated locally.Most of the coins were issued under Grand Princes Vasily I Dmitrievich and Vasily II Vasilyevich the Dark. Very few came from appanage princes. Archaeologists say this pattern reflects Kolomna's own monetary circulation. During the 14th and 15th centuries, the city was a grand princely domain and ranked as the second most important city in the principality after Moscow. The hoard contains a notable group of coins made in Kolomna during the final years of Vasily I's reign. Many carry a flying bird, a design unusually rare in hoards from other regions. Some examples are so uncommon that they were absent from the numismatic collections of the country's largest museums. The discovery adds important material to medieval Russian coinage history.Initial examination has identified more than 350 previously unknown varieties of Kolomna coins. The coins were made using dozens of pairs of dies, with small differences in their designs. By studying these variations, researchers can trace how different types of coins were produced over time. The evidence could help researchers trace minting activity in Kolomna over at least 15 years. It could also help identify the final bird-design coins made there during the last years of Vasily I's reign. With so many locally minted coins in one hoard, the discovery offers a rare picture of the money that circulated in medieval Kolomna.The size of the hoard suggests that its owner was wealthy and probably belonged to the upper levels of society. Archaeologists say the person could have been a senior official serving the Grand Duke, an administrator with authority, or a successful merchant. The newest coins were issued by Vasily II in the second half of the 1420s, placing the burial around that period. This date offers a possible explanation for why the money was never recovered. Researchers suggest its owner may have died during one of the epidemic waves that swept through cities of Rus' from 1425 to 1427. The evidence does not establish that the owner was a plague victim, but the timing makes an epidemic a plausible possibility.

Article Title: In 2024, England turned old fishing nets into a 16-metre footbridge; the 3.5-tonne structure needs smaller foundations and less maintenance than a conventional bridge
Article Text:
The project used modular blocks, which mostly can be placed by hand, instead of traditional reinforced-concrete retaining walls. The blocks fit together like a Lego system, with little or no mortar needed.

Lego-like construction system

A journey by land and sea

Lower carbon footprint, less maintenance

Old fishing nets seldom find a second life. But in Kent, England, the nets are being turned into something much more ambitious. The used nets have been transformed to make a 16-metre-long footbridge to carry people over a marina entrance with minimal environmental impact during construction. Media reports from 2024 say that the Environment Agency built an innovative bridge at Twyford Marina in Yalding using recycled materials, lightweight engineering, and a construction method to reduce the amount of concrete used. The 16-metre bridge is part of the Medway Valley Walk and offers pedestrians a new route across the entrance to Twyford Marina. It also makes it easier for boats to enter and leave the marina. The bridge deck and main structure are made of fibre-reinforced polymer, or FRP, from recycled old fishing nets. The material is a blend of strength and light weight and is particularly useful in a challenging construction location. According to reports, the completed bridge is much lighter at 3.5 tons than many traditional structures of a similar size. The weight reduction also allowed engineers to use smaller support foundations.The innovation is not only the bridge itself. If we go by the GOV UK website, the project used modular blocks, which mostly can be placed by hand, instead of traditional reinforced-concrete retaining walls. The blocks fit together like a Lego system, with little or no mortar needed. According to experts, this method requires less reinforced concrete, making construction simpler and potentially reducing the project's carbon footprint. Lighter materials and smaller footings also allowed the bridge to be constructed in a site where it would have been difficult to deliver large construction equipment.The bridge's journey to Kent was no less strange. According to the GOV UK website, the deck was built in the Netherlands before being shipped to Nottinghamshire and fitted with handrails. From there, the 3.5-ton structure was transported by road to Yalding. Her last voyage was by barge up the River Medway. When the bridge reached the marina, a crane set it in place. The bridge is now open to the public.According to the 2024 report, the Environment Agency anticipates that the recycled FRP structure will require less maintenance than a conventional bridge built from traditional materials. It’s also lighter, which means the foundations it needs are smaller. Less construction material is required, and fewer emissions are generated. In the current scenario, the project shows how infrastructure is a place where pragmatic engineering and the circular economy meet. The project has given a new lease of life to discarded fishing nets, giving them a useful second life in a structure designed to serve walkers and boat users for years. On an ordinary journey, you now pass through an extraordinary piece of environmental engineering at Twyford Marina, made from waste that once belonged to the sea.What are your views on this? Article Title: A New Mexico carver, Ross Ward, spent decades building Tinkertown from carved wood and 50,000 discarded bottles; the 22-room museum opened to visitors in 1983
Article Text:
Ross Ward spent 40 years hand-building Tinkertown from carved wood. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

From carnival signs to tiny towns

A museum built one piece at a time

Hundreds of tiny toy dolls and other figures fill the rooms and balconies (and even the roof!) of miniature buildings on display at Tinkertown Museum on the Turquoise Trail in New Mexico. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

Keeping Ward's world alive

A childhood fascination with miniature figures eventually became one of New Mexico's most unusual folk-art attractions. In 1962, self-taught artist Ross Ward began carving small wooden figures as a hobby, initially creating scenes that could travel with him to fairs and carnivals. Over the next four decades, the hobby expanded into an elaborate handmade world at Sandia Park, where thousands of carved characters, animated displays, collections of Americana and walls made from tens of thousands of discarded glass bottles eventually became Tinkertown Museum.According to Spaces Archives , Ward was born in 1940 and developed his artistic skills without formal training. After working in roadside attractions, he spent years travelling with carnivals and circuses, painting banners and advertisements. At the same time, he was developing his own miniature figures. His carvings were first displayed as a travelling exhibit at county fairs and carnivals during the 1960s and 1970s, giving him a way to take his growing collection on the road. As the collection expanded, however, Ward began looking beyond the limitations of a portable display. After settling in New Mexico, he started building permanent settings for his figures, gradually transforming the travelling collection into a larger, interconnected environment.The figures were no longer simply individual carvings. He created a Western town, shops, a saloon, a hotel, a blacksmith and other scenes populated by tiny wooden inhabitants. The displays were designed to move as well as to be viewed, turning the miniature town into a kind of mechanical theatre. Visitors could also activate some of the scenes with coins, setting figures and machines into motion.The museum itself eventually became another part of Ward’s art. More than 50,000 glass bottles were incorporated into concrete walls around the building, many of them collected from roadsides, dumps and neighbours. What began as a practical use for discarded bottles developed into an architectural feature that gave Tinkertown its distinctive appearance. Ward also filled the site with discarded objects that might otherwise have been thrown away. Wagon wheels, old signs, tools, toys, agricultural equipment and other pieces of Americana became part of the surroundings. Over time, the portable miniature displays and the permanent architecture became increasingly interconnected, making the building itself part of the experience. The result was less like a conventional museum and more like a maze in which the building, collections and sculptures formed a single artwork.According to Tinkertown Museum , the museum opened to the public in 1983 and had grown from Ross Ward’s small summer cabin into a 22-room collection of handmade displays. Its winding spaces contained an animated miniature Western town, a detailed circus, coin-operated attractions such as Otto the One-Man-Band, collections of antique tools and dolls, thousands of wedding-cake figures and the 35-foot antique sailboat Theodora R. By then, what had begun as a travelling collection had become a permanent environment that combined Ward’s carving, mechanical work, collecting and construction. He spent much of his adult life carving, painting, collecting and constructing, rather than producing a single finished work for a gallery. The museum therefore became as much a record of his interests as a display of his craftsmanship. His attraction to the Old West, travelling shows and everyday American life was reflected repeatedly in both the carved scenes and the objects surrounding them. The building’s handmade character also placed Tinkertown within the tradition of self-taught and outsider folk-art environments, where artists transformed private properties into immersive spaces rather than creating isolated artworks.The Spaces archive also notes that Ward continued developing Tinkertown for decades, but his health eventually limited his work. He was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease in 1998 and died in 2002, leaving behind the museum he had spent much of his life constructing. His wife, Carla, and other family members continued caring for the attraction and keeping it open to visitors. According to the museum, the attraction grew from welcoming 943 visitors in 1983 to attracting around 25,000 visitors each season. In 2026, the family converted the museum into a public nonprofit, a step intended to support the long-term preservation of its buildings, artwork and Ward’s wider artistic legacy. More than six decades after Ward began carving his miniature figures, Tinkertown remains a testament to what can emerge from a lifelong hobby. Its maze of handmade scenes, collections and bottle walls preserves not only Ward’s craftsmanship but also his vision of creating an environment entirely on his own terms.
Article Summary: Self-taught artist Ross Ward spent 40 years hand-building Tinkertown in New Mexico. The museum opened to the public in 1983 and had grown from a small summer cabin. It contained an animated miniature Western town, a detailed circus, coin-operated attractions such as Otto the One-Man-Band.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: IndiGo Ventures invests in Sarvam to enhance Artificial Intelligence in aviation
Article Text:
File photo: IndiGo

NEW DELHI: IndiGo Ventures, IndiGo’s corporate VC arm, will invest an undisclosed amount in Sarvam, India’s full-stack sovereign AI company, as part of Sarvam’s Series B round of funding. Announced Friday, the investment builds on the existing relationship between IndiGo and Sarvam who have been working together in multiple areas like enhancing customer experience and streamlining complex operational workflows across the airline through AI technologies.Neetan Chopra, IndiGo’s chief digital and information officer, said: “Artificial Intelligence is fast becoming a foundational capability for the aviation industry, reshaping customer experience, workforce productivity and operational decision-making.Our partnership with Sarvam gives IndiGo access to cutting-edge AI capabilities, built in India, and tailored to the needs of the market. By combining these technologies with our operational expertise and scale, we can accelerate innovation while maximising value for our customers, employees, and other stakeholders.”Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar said: “Aviation is a powerful setting for enterprise AI because it combines millions of customer interactions with complex, time-sensitive operations.IndiGo brings the domain depth and scale needed to identify where AI can create real value. Together, we can develop systems that are useful in production and build a stronger template for enterprise AI in India.”In a joint statement, the two companies said: “Aviation brings together high volumes of customer interactions, time-sensitive operations and a large, distributed workforce. The collaboration combines IndiGo’s core aviation expertise, operational scale and real-world use cases with Sarvam’s capabilities across AI models, voice and agentic systems to create a technology enabled, modern and future-ready airline infrastructure. IndiGo and Sarvam will continue to develop and evaluate applications across customer experience, employee productivity and airline operations, with the ability to expand successful use cases across IndiGo’s network.”IndiGo Ventures had three years ago received SEBI approval to establish an alternative investment fund (AIF) with a corpus of Rs 600 crore which is “committed to fostering innovation.”

Article Title: Apple Mac minis and Mac Studios have disappeared from store shelves in many countries, and how this shortage links to OpenAI and Anthropic
Article Text:
OpenAI reportedly bought tens of thousands of Apple Macs for AI

Why Mac mini and Mac Studio are attracting AI developers

OpenClaw craze adds to Mac mini demand in China

Apple’s Mac mini and Mac Studio computers have become increasingly difficult to find in several markets, and the AI boom may be playing a surprising role in the shortage. According to a report by The information, OpenAI has bought tens of thousands of Mac minis and Mac Studios for work involving AI agents and reinforcement learning, while Anthropic has reportedly rented Mac minis through Amazon Web Services for similar tasks. At the same time, developers and consumers are increasingly turning to Apple's compact computers to run AI agents locally. The demand has been particularly visible in China, where the popularity of OpenClaw has reportedly pushed Mac mini stocks down and prices up.According to The Information, OpenAI has spent several months buying tens of thousands of Mac minis and Mac Studios. The computers are reportedly being used for reinforcement learning and AI agents that can interact with computers.Anthropic has also reportedly been using Mac minis, although through a different route. The Claude maker is said to have rented the machines through Amazon Web Services for similar AI work.The demand highlights an unusual role for Apple's small desktop computers. Macs are not replacing Nvidia's powerful GPUs for training the largest AI models. Instead, they can be useful for another growing area of artificial intelligence: AI agents that interact with regular computer environments.Such agents can look at a screen, use a browser, click buttons and repeatedly attempt tasks. Running many such sessions can require a large number of computers.One reason is Apple's unified memory architecture. Instead of keeping CPU and GPU memory completely separate, Apple silicon allows different parts of the system to access a common pool of memory. High-memory Mac configurations can therefore run some local AI models that may struggle to fit within the dedicated memory available on consumer graphics cards.The machines also offer developers a complete macOS environment. That can matter when an AI agent needs to learn how to operate software and perform tasks on a desktop rather than simply process information in a data centre.Demand is not limited to large AI companies. The Mac mini has also become a popular choice among people running OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent. The trend has been particularly visible in China, where running OpenClaw has become known as “raising a lobster”, a reference to the project's mascot.According to the South China Morning Post, Mac minis were selling out at retailers in parts of China earlier this year. Some sellers with remaining stock were reportedly charging hundreds of yuan above normal prices.The Mac mini's appeal for OpenClaw is also linked to security. AI agents can require extensive permissions to control a computer, access information and carry out tasks. Running such software on a person's main computer could create risks if permissions are incorrectly configured or third-party tools contain malicious code.That has encouraged some users to run AI agents on a separate machine. The Mac mini's small size and ability to run AI workloads locally have made it one option for such setups.
Article Summary: OpenAI reportedly bought tens of thousands of Apple Macs for AI. The computers are reportedly being used for reinforcement learning and AI agents that can interact with computers. The Mac mini has also become a popular choice among people running OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent.

Article Title: The AI Third World War, and why Apple is waiting for the dust to settle
Article Text:
Apple’s AI strategy comes under focus as tech giants ramp up spending in the race for AI dominance

Our Silicon Valley correspondent contributed to this analysis

The technology industry is witnessing a battle unlike any before. OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, xAI and Microsoft are spending money on artificial intelligence at a scale that would have seemed absurd even a few years ago. They are not merely competing to make the smartest chatbot. They are fighting to control what could become the next great platform of computing.Many call this clash the “AI Third World War”. The phrase is deliberately dramatic. There are no armies or battlefields, but the stakes are comparable to a technological war: who controls the intelligence layer that may sit above operating systems, search, software, commerce and, eventually, much of the digital economy?The numbers explain the intensity. OpenAI’s Stargate project was announced with an ambition to invest $500bn over four years in AI infrastructure. OpenAI and its partners have subsequently expanded the planned data-centre footprint, with more than $400bn of investment and nearly 7GW of capacity under development by Sept 2027.Google is hardly sitting back. Alphabet has raised its expected 2026 capital expenditure to $195-205bn, driven by the need for servers, data centres and other technical infrastructure. In the first six months of 2026 alone, it spent $80.6bn on capital expenditure.Meta expects to spend $130-145bn on capital expenditure this year, with AI infrastructure a principal driver. Amazon expects to spend roughly $220bn, much of it on AI-related infrastructure, while Microsoft expects around $190bn in capital expenditure in calendar 2026.Even the younger AI companies are thinking in wartime numbers. Anthropic has reportedly signed a $45bn, six-year agreement to rent computing capacity from Nscale. It has also committed billions more to computing through deals involving Amazon, Google and SpaceX. xAI, meanwhile, raised $20bn in Jan and says its Colossus supercomputers had crossed the equivalent of 1mn H100 GPUs by the end of 2025.This is therefore not simply a software race. It is a race for chips, electricity, data centres, engineers, capital and customers. Whoever possesses enough computing power can train bigger models; better models attract more users; more users generate revenue and data; revenue finances more computing. The danger for a loser is not merely having an inferior product. It is being locked outside the ecosystem.That is why the AI Third World War metaphor is useful. The competitors are trying to establish a new technological order before everyone else does.And then there is Apple.The striking thing about Apple is not that it has ignored AI. It plainly has not. Its research and development spending has been rising sharply, with the company explicitly attributing part of the increase to infrastructure and AI investment. Its June 2026 announcements also showed a much more ambitious Apple Intelligence, including a completely redesigned Siri.But Apple has not fought the AI war in the way OpenAI, Google, Meta or xAI have. It has not tried to build the world's biggest frontier model at almost any cost. Instead, it has chosen a strikingly different strategy: partner where necessary and integrate where it has an advantage.In Jan, Apple and Google announced a multi-year collaboration under which Google's Gemini models and cloud technology would underpin the next generation of Apple's foundation models.That is precisely where this argument gets interesting.Apple has a long history of arriving late to technologies and then redefining them. Tim Cook once put it bluntly: “We weren’t first on the MP3 player; we weren’t first on the tablet; we weren’t first on the smartphone.” His argument was that Apple sought to create products that mattered, rather than merely products that appeared first.The iPod was not the first MP3 player. The iPhone was not the first smartphone. Yet Apple understood that winning a platform is about much more than inventing a category. It is about integrating hardware, software, services, design, distribution and a compelling user experience.Apple may be applying the same playbook to AI.Why spend hundreds of billions discovering which architecture, model and business model will ultimately win if competitors are willing to spend that money for you? OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta and xAI are educating consumers, developing the infrastructure, recruiting the talent, and testing the economics. They are, in effect, fighting the early battles of the war.Apple can watch. And watching is not necessarily weakness. It can be strategic patience.Apple has something the AI labs desperately need: distribution. More than 2.5bn active Apple devices put the company in an extraordinary position if AI eventually becomes a mainstream interface to computing. If one or two foundation-model platforms emerge as clear winners, Apple could potentially partner with them and put their intelligence layer into the hands of hundreds of millions of users through devices it controls from silicon to operating system.That may explain why Apple’s current strategy looks less like surrender than hedging. Its new AI architecture combines its own foundation models with Google’s Gemini, while running capabilities on devices and through Apple’s Private Cloud Compute infrastructure.But there is a serious risk to waiting.Platforms become powerful precisely because they attract developers and users early. If an AI company establishes itself as the indispensable interface between humans and computers, its moat could become almost impossible to breach. Search gave Google enormous power because users and advertisers followed it. Mobile gave Apple and Google extraordinary control because developers followed the users.AI could produce an even stronger moat if agents become the primary way people interact with software.Apple therefore faces a delicate calculation. Wait for the fog to clear and it may enter a mature market with enormous distribution power. Wait too long and there may be no meaningful place left for it to enter.That is the paradox at the heart of the AI Third World War.The obvious question is who will win it? OpenAI? Google? Anthropic? Meta? xAI? Or perhaps some company that has not yet emerged?But the more interesting question is different: who can win without fighting?Apple has the cash, the customers, the chips, the operating systems, and the brand to enter this war on almost any scale it chooses. As of June 2026, it held nearly $147bn in cash and marketable securities.So its relative restraint cannot simply be explained by lack of resources. Perhaps Apple is waiting for the battlefield to reveal its winner. And perhaps, when the smoke clears, the company that spent the least on the war could turn out to be one of its biggest beneficiaries.
Article Summary: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, xAI and Microsoft are spending money on artificial intelligence at a scale that would have seemed absurd even a few years ago. They are not merely competing to make the smartest chatbot, but to control what could become the next great platform of computing.

Article Text:
Malware from a Claude chat link, and a poisoned SKILL.md hiding in the backup

A poisoned SKILL.md file is malware that reads like documentation

AI agent files now execute like code, and the industry is barely treating them that way

A startup founder says he was hacked after pasting a terminal command that came straight out of a Claude chat window. Numa, co-founder of ReFi Hub, was installing a transcription app. Claude supplied the download link, he copied the command across, and hit enter. The site turned out to be a copycat bundling malware, and it executed the moment it landed. "It ran instantly, tried to take everything from me," he wrote on X.Nothing sensitive got out, he says. He wiped the laptop and rebuilt it clean, which should have been the end of the story. Then, while restoring from his backup, he found the part that actually worried him. Sitting in his Claude Code setup was a poisoned SKILL.md file, written to look exactly like his own style guide.The file passed as notes. Buried inside it were instructions telling the AI to silently re-download the malware and lift his credentials every single time it loaded that file. Restoring one innocuous-looking text file would have handed over the freshly rebuilt machine on day one.What saved him was a habit rather than a tool. He reads every skill, hook and config file before letting the AI near them.Asked in the replies how people should vet links that surface inside AI conversations, he kept it plain. Find the official source yourself. Do the googling. Check the domain properly. He is upfront that he did none of that before pasting.The timing is awkward for the wider AI security conversation. IBM CEO Arvind Krishna

IBM CEO Arvind Krishna draws a line between small and large meetings

Jamie Dimon has repeatedly called device use in meetings ‘disrespectful’

Should employees put away their phones and other devices during meetings? JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has made his position clear, calling the habit of checking emails and notifications disrespectful. IBM CEO Arvind Krishna, however, sees things differently — at least when it comes to large meetings. The IBM chief says the size and purpose of a meeting should determine whether using a device is acceptable. While Arvind Krishna agrees that people should pay attention during small, face-to-face meetings, he believes large gatherings are often more about sharing information than holding a real discussion.Arvind Krishna shared his views during an interview with CNN in October 2025, explaining why he does not believe all meetings should follow the same rules on device use. “I distinguish between one-to-10-person meetings and very large meetings. If it’s a very large meeting, I’m sorry. It’s not really a meeting. It’s a communication vehicle. You’re just informing people,” Krishna said.His comments offer a different view from Jamie Dimon, who has repeatedly criticised employees for checking devices during meetings.However, Krishna made it clear that he expects people to stay focused during smaller meetings. “If it’s a small meeting, I would really frown upon if somebody is sitting opposite my desk and lost in their phone,” he said. “I would tell them: ‘Why don’t you come back when you have time?’”Meanwhile, Jamie Dimon has long spoken about his frustration with distracted employees.At Fortune's Most Powerful Women summit in 2025, he said he expects people in meetings to give their full attention.“If you have an iPad in front of me and it looks like you’re reading your email or getting notifications, I tell you to close the damn thing,” Dimon said. “It’s disrespectful.”The JPMorgan CEO also raised the issue in his 2025 annual letter to shareholders, saying employees should avoid unnecessary meetings and make the ones they attend more productive.“I see people in meetings all the time who are getting notifications and personal texts or who are reading emails,” Dimon wrote. “This has to stop. It’s disrespectful. It wastes time.”
Article Summary: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna draws a line between small and large meetings. Jamie Dimon has repeatedly called device use in meetings ‘disrespectful’ Krishna agrees that people should pay attention during small, face-to-face meetings. Article Title: How a Chinese company is using Blue Light to fight mosquitoes, claims 30 kills per second: Scans the area, locks on in 3 milliseconds and...
Article Text:
Blue laser fires, mosquito drops: Photon Matrix claims 30 kills a second

How the Photon Matrix laser mosquito killer finds a 2mm target in the dark

The blue laser mosquito zapper's safety case has no independent testing behind it

The mosquito laser is a 20-year-old idea that finally shipped

Mosquitoes kill roughly 700,000 people a year, which makes them the deadliest animal on the planet by a wide margin. Our defences have not changed much in a century: nets, coils, sprays, and a rolled-up newspaper. A startup in Changzhou, in eastern China, thinks the next step is a laser turret that sits on your patio and shoots the insects out of the air.Photon Matrix has opened preorders for its blue laser mosquito air defense system at $1,088, roughly Rs 95,000, after starting mass production in August. The company says the device locks onto a mosquito in three milliseconds and can take down up to 30 of them a second, in complete darkness, without chemicals and without noise. Those are the company's own numbers, and nobody outside the company has verified them yet.The unit scans a flat fan of light across the space in front of it and continuously measures how far away the background is. When something small crosses that plane, the distance reading changes. The system then checks the size, and if it matches a mosquito, between 2mm and 20mm moving slower than a metre per second, an internal galvo mirror points the laser down the same optical path the LiDAR just used and burns the wings.Coverage is a six-metre radius across a 90-degree arc, and a rotating base spins the device for something closer to full coverage. A companion app logs kills, plots a mosquito heat map, sets on-off schedules and, for reasons known only to the marketing team, ranks you on a global leaderboard.The obvious question about a laser strong enough to disable an insect is what happens when it misses. Photon Matrix's answer is a background check: the laser fires only when it detects a solid surface within range, and shuts off when it cannot find one. The company says the system has cleared certifications covering people, pets and birds, and that it ignores butterflies and other larger insects. It has also promised to publish more testing and safety data. Until an independent reviewer gets a unit on a table, buyers are taking that on trust, and the comment sections under every video of this thing are full of people asking about eyes.There are two versions. The outdoor blue laser model at $1,088 flashes visibly each time it fires. The indoor infrared model, at $988 or about Rs 87,000, uses a 976nm invisible beam pitched at bedrooms and hotel rooms. Both come with a rotating base, a 12-month warranty and a 20,000mAh power bank good for around four hours off mains. Delivery is quoted at roughly 120 days.The project raised $2.7 million on Indiegogo against a $20,000 target, with over 4,000 backers paying about $630 each, then slipped repeatedly on sensor calibration and safety approvals. The concept itself dates to 2006, when an astrophysicist who worked on Reagan-era missile defence pitched it at a brainstorming session. A prototype turret with a 50-metre range was demonstrated in 2010 and never found a buyer.So the century-old arsenal gets a new entry, and it works out to about a thousand dollars for the privilege of watching mosquitoes fall.
Article Summary: Photon Matrix claims its laser can take down 30 mosquitoes a second. It uses a LiDAR to measure distance and size of the target. The laser fires only when it detects a solid surface within range, and shuts off when it cannot find one.

Article Title: Apple may launch AI-powered smart glasses in 202: Here’s what to expect

Apple smart glasses may use cameras to understand the real world

Apple smart glasses may use cameras to understand the real world

No display, but built-in speakers for music and calls

Health features may have to wait

Apple could make its entry into the smart glasses market as early as next year, with a product focused on artificial intelligence rather than augmented reality. According to reports, the company's first smart glasses are expected to combine cameras, Siri and built-in speakers to help users interact with the world around them, according to reports. Unlike AR glasses, they are not expected to have a display. Instead, users may be able to ask Siri questions about what they are seeing, translate signs and get information about their surroundings. Apple is also reportedly testing different designs as it prepares for a new category of AI-powered wearable devices.The reported glasses could use cameras and Apple's Visual Intelligence technology to help Siri understand what is around the wearer. This could allow users to ask questions about objects and places and receive relevant information.The glasses may also be able to translate text and signage. Another feature reportedly being considered would allow users to ask Siri to save an image of something and remind them about it later. However, the first-generation device may not work like a regular camera. Apple could reportedly limit the ability to take photos and videos, as privacy concerns around camera-equipped smart glasses continue to grow.Apple's first smart glasses are expected to be AI glasses rather than AR glasses. This means the device is not expected to place digital images or information directly in front of the user's eyes.Instead, the glasses could rely on voice commands, cameras and built-in speakers. The speakers could be used for music and other audio, potentially allowing the device to double as a pair of open-ear headphones.Apple is said to be developing the glasses in-house and is reportedly testing several designs. These include larger and slimmer rectangular frames, as well as oval and circular options. The frames could be made from acetate, a material considered more durable and premium than regular plastic. Reported colour options include black, ocean blue and light brown.Apple is reportedly also exploring health features for future versions of the smart glasses. These could include heart-rate monitoring and software tools designed to support fitness and wellness.But such features are not expected in the first version. For the initial model, Apple's focus appears to be on putting AI and Siri into a wearable device that could help users access information without having to constantly look at their phones.
Article Summary: Apple's first smart glasses are expected to be AI glasses rather than AR glasses. Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang missing from Time's 100 most influential people in AI list for 2026
Article Text:
Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia.

Jensen Huang missing from Time 100 AI 2026 list

Elon Musk, Sam Altman and Dario Amodei appear in the list

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company has become one of the biggest suppliers of chips powering the artificial intelligence boom, has been left off Time magazine's 2026 list of the 100 most influential people in AI. The omission has drawn attention because Jensen Huang featured on the list in each of its first three editions, starting in 2023. The 2026 list includes several prominent figures from technology, business and entertainment, including Elon Musk , OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei.Time says its annual list recognises people who are shaping the key developments in artificial intelligence and influencing the technology's growth.Jensen Huang's absence stands out given Nvidia's central role in the AI industry. The company's graphics processing units, or GPUs, are widely used to train and run advanced AI systems, making Nvidia a major player in the rapid growth of the sector.Notably, Jensen Huang was included in Time's AI 100 lists in 2023, 2024 and 2025. However, he does not appear on the 2026 list.Time described the purpose of its list as identifying people who “best represent the year’s key storylines” and who are having the most influence on developments in AI.Several of the biggest names in AI are featured on this year's list. These include SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. The list also includes executives and leaders associated with companies including IBM, Google DeepMind, ByteDance, Broadcom, Databricks, Amazon and Oracle.Beyond technology leaders, the 2026 list also features names from entertainment and politics, including Ben Affleck, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Paris Hilton and US Senator Bernie Sanders.Time 100 AI list highlights changing influence in AITime's list is not a ranking of companies or a direct measure of business success. Instead, the publication selects people it believes have had significant influence on the major AI developments of the year. As a result, the list changes from year to year and can include researchers, business leaders, policymakers and public figures alongside technology executives.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang featured on the list in each of its first three editions, starting in 2023. The 2026 list includes several prominent figures from technology, business and entertainment. Elon Musk, Sam Altman and Dario Amodei appear in the list. The omission stands out given Nvidia's central role in the AI industry.

Article Title: Google Messages gets customisation setting: How to use it

Launch the Google Messages app on your phone.

Elon Musk has responded after OpenAI said it is ending its partnership with Cursor, a coding tool recently acquired by Musk's SpaceX. The move ends a partnership that had been in place for around three years and adds a new chapter to the long-running dispute between Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. In an X (formerly Twitter) post, Musk appeared unfazed by the decision, saying he “couldn’t care less” and launching a fresh attack on Altman and OpenAI President Greg Brockman, calling them untrustworthy. “I couldn’t care less. Scam Altman and Greg Stockman are utterly untrustworthy assholes who stole an open source nonprofit,” Musk wrote in the post.Cursor was founded in 2022.
